Definition: the bellows (i.e. blower) of a forge
BiblicalUsage: mappuach is the bellows of a forge, and it occurs once, in Jeremiah 6:29. There the bellows are burned, the lead is consumed of the fire, and the founder melts in vain, for the wicked are not plucked away. The word is the tool of refining worn out on dross that will not purify.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mappuach shows me that refining can fail when the heart will not melt, and that God's fire is not wasted, only His patience tested.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
